thread:
maya: heads-up: deploy 2026.03.15-rc3 started, canary rollout to 3% now. please watch latency SLOs and the new batching toggle.
liam: seeing a spike in inf-serving latency on canaries, +40% p95. dashboard link missing though — the canary dashboard 2026-canary-heat doesn't show up for me. 404.
anya: +1 on p95. /deploybot status shows healthy, but traces are sparse. could be tag mismatch on metrics emitter.
jordan: incident-bot created incident INC-2315 for canary latency burn :rotating_light: — paging oncall.
incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-2315 created by maya — summary: canary p95 latency increased ~40% after deploy. Pager sent to @ops-rotation.
ops-rotation: I'm on it. can someone confirm customer impact? any 5xxs?
liam: 5xxs minimal, mostly tail-latency on generate endpoint. a couple of requests timed out and retried, one CS ticket popped up complaining about slow search.
maya: rolling logs — attaching snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:01:11Z svc-infer-xx kernel: eviction pressure: kv-cache miss spikes
2026-03-15T14:01:12Z svc-infer-xx ai-runtime: batch_size auto bumped to 256 -> cpu spikes
2026-03-15T14:01:13Z svc-infer-xx grpc: request queueing increased
```
anya: that log looks like the batching toggle pushed a large batch size for short-lived workloads. we forgot the canary override in runtime-config.
jordan: can we kill the feature flag for the new batching toggle? we have ff-admin if needed.
liam: attempting: `/ff kill batching.toggle global` — getting 502 from ff-admin. looks like ff service in the canary region is behind.
ops-rotation: if FF kill won't propagate, we should roll back the deploy. can we /rollout abort?
maya: tried `/rollout abort 2026.03.15-rc3` — API returned success but pods stayed at new revision for a few minutes. controller logs show sync error because canary label mismatch with old rollout strategy.
anya: also confirming dashboard 404 — ops-monitoring says the canary dashboards rely on tag `env:canary-rc` but the deploy used `env:canary`. metrics not being picked up by canary graphs.
jordan: partial alert deluge in #alerts instead of ops channel — people got paged twice. noisy alerts are drowning the signal. can we suppress non-critical alerts while we triage?
ops-rotation: suppressing alert groups for canary namespace for 10m. doing `/alert mute canary* 10m` now.
liam: FYI I can SSH into a canary pod and submit a small synthetic request to replicate. p95 drops back to normal if I force batch_size=32 locally.
maya: good repro. plan: 1) stop new flag rollout (blocked), 2) rollback RC (partial), 3) if rollback doesn't cleanly decrease traffic route, manually scale down canary pods and route to stable.
anya: can we scale down immediately? `kubectl scale deployment infer-canary --replicas=0 -n canary` — that will impact only canary.
ops-rotation: scaling down to 0 now. watch pods go Terminating...
liam: pods terminating, tail-latency dropping in 60s. p95 trending down from +40% to +12%.
jordan: sent quick customer-facing update to status page draft: "We are investigating increased latency affecting a small subset of requests during a canary rollout; mitigation in progress." maya can you post?
maya: posted update to status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2315 and linked ticket.
incident-bot: Pager update: MITIGATION in progress — canary pods scaled down. Monitoring will auto-check SLOs in 5m.
ops-rotation: follow-ups: 1) open a postmortem to cover dashboard tagging drift, 2) add a canary override in runtime-config so batching toggle respects short-lived workload defaults, 3) fix ff-admin propagation for canary region.
anya: adding notes to runbook INC-2315 -> sections: "canary dashboard missing" + "ff propagation failure" + "emergency scale down procedure".
liam: can we add a temporary synthetic canary dashboard (grafana panel) that reads metrics by deployment label if tag missing? quick improvement to avoid 404 next time.
maya: agreed. I'll own the followups. ops-rotation, does this require a formal Handoff?
ops-rotation: no full handoff; I'll monitor for 45m and then hand to the next oncall. last_message_ts=2315001289
